## Purpose

Fixes #52607

`NixlConnector` is an alias for the pull connector. `NixlPushConnector` already exists, but the usage guide never mentioned it, so same-node / non-RDMA setups keep the slow READ path.

Docs only. Default is still pull.

## Changes

- Explain pull vs push names in `docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md`
- Use `NixlPushConnector` in the same-host examples
- Point to the existing push design doc
- Short note on the connector list in `docs/features/disagg_prefill.md`

## Test plan

- [x] Docs-only; no code change
- [ ] Check the rendered usage page once docs CI is up

🚀
As the OG reporter for #52607. LGTM.

Suggestion for the new **Pull vs Push** section (optional, please merge without it if you'd rather not grow the section!)

**Context.** I was running the two-instance disaggregated-prefill setup from the usage guide on a rented two-GPU pod — one prefiller on GPU 0, one decoder on GPU 1, the default `NixlConnector` on both, the repo's `toy_proxy_server.py` in front — and pushing a small benchmark through it at three prompt lengths. 

As part of the run, I had planned a check of which UCX transport was actually carrying the KV cache. In my run nothing announced it: clean bring-up, `NIXL compatibility check passed`, all 49 completions through the toy proxy returned 200, plausible-looking throughput — and the KV cache was crossing TCP the whole time.

The section tells a reader which connector to choose, but not how to check which path they actually got. 

Proposed addition:

> **Checking which transport you got.** Start both instances once with `UCX_PROTO_INFO=y`. In the log, find the protocol rows whose title mentions `cuda` — e.g. `remote memory read by ucp_get*(multi) into cuda/GPU0 from cuda` — and read the transport in the right-hand column. If it names `tcp/...`, the KV cache is crossing TCP rather than `cuda_ipc` (in my run the row printed `software emulation | tcp/eth0`). Note that `cuda_ipc` can appear in the advertised list — `device(cuda_ipc/cuda)  am(tcp/eth0 cma/memory cuda_ipc/cuda)` — without ever being selected; advertised is not selected. The consumer's `KV Transfer metrics ... Throughput (MB/s)` line (per transfer) gives a number to sanity-check against your hardware class, and `nvidia-smi topo -p2p r` shows whether peer access exists at all.
@rayhanmemon, explicitly enabling `cuda_ipc` for get using `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` should help selecting `cuda_ipc` for the READ case, could you please confirm?

Friendly bump for review. Docs-only; issue reporter already LGTM'd.

@tvegas1 on the `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` note: happy to add a one-liner under Pull vs push if that is the recommended workaround for pull on same-node. Prefer keeping this PR docs-only unless you want that included here.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @Atharv-16.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

> 
> @tvegas1 on the `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` note: happy to add a one-liner under Pull vs push if that is the recommended workaround for pull on same-node. Prefer keeping this PR docs-only unless you want that included here.

I’d suggest keeping the push documentation, but avoiding a blanket recommendation to replace pull/READ with push on same-node setups solely because CUDA IPC GET was previously disabled. NIXL 1.5 enables CUDA IPC GET by default ([ai-dynamo/nixl#2208](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2208)); for older versions, the environment variable is a workaround that can be documented.

Rebased onto latest main.

Updated the docs per @tvegas1's feedback: kept the NixlPushConnector same-node docs, dropped the blanket "replace pull with push" recommendation, and noted that NIXL 1.5 enables CUDA IPC GET by default ([nixl#2208](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2208)), with `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` as the workaround on older NIXL for pull/READ on the same node.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -21,7 +21,7 @@ Now supports 9 types of connectors:
 
 - **ExampleConnector**: refer to [examples/disaggregated/example_connector/run.sh](../../examples/disaggregated/example_connector/run.sh) for the example usage of ExampleConnector disaggregated prefilling.
 - **LMCacheConnectorV1**: refer to [examples/disaggregated/lmcache/disagg_prefill_lmcache_v1/disagg_example_nixl.sh](../../examples/disaggregated/lmcache/disagg_prefill_lmcache_v1/disagg_example_nixl.sh) for the example usage of LMCacheConnectorV1 disaggregated prefilling which uses NIXL as the underlying KV transmission. LMCache also offers a multi-process (MP) mode via `LMCacheMPConnector`, where a standalone `lmcache server` holds the KV cache shared by one or more vLLM instances; see the [LMCache examples](../../examples/disaggregated/lmcache/README.md) and the [LMCache docs](https://docs.lmcache.ai) for setup.
-- **NixlConnector**: refer to [tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh](../../tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh) for the example usage of NixlConnector disaggregated prefilling which support fully async send/recv. For detailed usage guide, see [NixlConnector Usage Guide](nixl_connector_usage.md). For feature compatibility details, see [NixlConnector Compatibility Matrix](nixl_connector_compatibility.md). You may specify one or multiple NIXL transfer backends, such as:
+- **NixlConnector**: refer to [tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh](../../tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh) for the example usage of NixlConnector disaggregated prefilling which support fully async send/recv. `NixlConnector` is the pull alias (`NixlPullConnector`); `NixlPushConnector` is also available. For same-node CUDA IPC GET (NIXL 1.5+ default, or `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` on older NIXL) and when to use push, see [Pull vs push](nixl_connector_usage.md#pull-vs-push) in the [NixlConnector Usage Guide](nixl_connector_usage.md). For feature compatibility details, see [NixlConnector Compatibility Matrix](nixl_connector_compatibility.md). You may specify one or multiple NIXL transfer backends, such as:
 
   ```bash
   --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both", "kv_buffer_device":"cuda", "kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX", "GDS"]}}'

@@ -2,6 +2,8 @@
 
 NixlConnector is a high-performance KV cache transfer connector for vLLM's disaggregated prefilling feature. It provides fully asynchronous send/receive operations using the NIXL library for efficient cross-process KV cache transfer.
 
+`NixlConnector` is a backward-compatible alias for `NixlPullConnector`. vLLM also ships `NixlPushConnector`. See [Pull vs push](#pull-vs-push) for which name to use.
+
 For feature compatibility details (supported model architectures, TP configurations, and feature interactions), see the [NixlConnector Compatibility Matrix](nixl_connector_compatibility.md).
 
 ## Prerequisites
@@ -76,8 +78,26 @@ vllm serve <MODEL> \
   }'
 ```
 
+## Pull vs push
+
+vLLM registers three NIXL connector names:
+
+| Name | Behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| `NixlPullConnector` | Decode reads KV from prefill with NIXL READ |
+| `NixlConnector` | Alias for `NixlPullConnector` (the default name in examples) |
+| `NixlPushConnector` | Prefill writes KV into decode memory with NIXL WRITE |
+
+On InfiniBand or RoCE, READ and WRITE are both line-rate, so pull is a reasonable default.
+
+Same-node pull over UCX `cuda_ipc` needs CUDA IPC GET. NIXL 1.5 enables CUDA IPC GET by default ([nixl#2208](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2208)). On older NIXL, set `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` if you want pull/READ on the same node. `NixlPushConnector` is still available when WRITE fits your layout better; use the same connector name on both instances. Mixing pull and push is not supported.
+
+For the push design, see [NIXL push-mode KV transfer](../design/nixl_kv_push_connector.md).
+
 ## Basic Usage (on the same host)
 
+The examples below use `NixlPushConnector` on a same-host layout. You can keep `"kv_connector":"NixlConnector"` (pull) on the same node with NIXL 1.5+, or with `UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_GET_ZCOPY=on` on older NIXL.
+
 ### Producer (Prefiller) Configuration
 
 Start a prefiller instance that produces KV caches
@@ -90,7 +110,7 @@ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 \
 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
   --port 8100 \
   --enforce-eager \
-  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
+  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
 ```
 
 ### Consumer (Decoder) Configuration
@@ -105,7 +125,7 @@ VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 \
 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
   --port 8200 \
   --enforce-eager \
-  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
+  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
 ```
 
 ### Proxy Server
